# Tutorial: c4h_save

## Overview and objectives

The goal of c4h_save is to export climate data objects into various file formats (e.g., CSV, NetCDF, GeoTIFF, or RDS) for storage, sharing, or future analysis. This step ensures that processed data and results are preserved in standardized.

# Tutorial: c4h_convert

<img src="figures/general/logo_harmonize.png" align="left" height="50"/></a> <img src="figures/general/logo_bsc.png" align="left" height="50"/></a> <img src="figures/general/logo_clim4health.svg" align="center" height="50" width="100"/></a>

## Overview and objectives

Inside clim4health is a function to convert data objects. The goal of convert is to transform the climate data object into different formats. This step facilitates data exchange and integration with external tools and ensures compatibility with different modeling or visualization platforms.

## Load the data

``` r
fcst_path <- "inst/extdata/forecast/"
fcst_path <- paste0(fcst_path)

fcst <- clim4health::c4h_load(fcst_path,
                             variable = "t2m",
                             year = 2025,
                             month = 1,
                             ext = 'nc'
                            )
```

## Save terra files

``` r
obj_terra <- clim4health:::c4h_convert(fcst, 's2dv', 'terra')
clim4health:::c4h_save(obj_terra, "terra", "resutl.tif")
```

## Save csv files

``` r
obj_csv <- clim4health:::c4h_convert(fcst, 's2dv', 'csv')
clim4health:::c4h_save(obj_csv, 'csv', "result.csv")
```

## Save polygons files

``` r
obj_polygons <- clim4health:::c4h_convert(fcst, 's2dv', 'polygons')
clim4health:::c4h_save(obj_polygons, "polygons", "result.gpkg")
```
